questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me to go somewhere I had never been before and then it felt very comforting that Australia is an English speaking country. Besides from that I wanted to meet different cultures.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was super easy and any questions were answered by the administration of my university

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: they threw an introductionary week with fun activities and a party which was great in order to get to know a lot of people

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky. I never even went on an inspection because a girl I met in the O-week (intro week) had a room available in her flat and that was the best decision ever!! Although I heard it was very troubling for others to find a nice, clean AND cheap accommodation, buuuut I would recommend you to lower your standards for the accommodation if you are on a budget!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: living off campus was the best thing to do in this case! I only heard horror stories about living on campus (at Griffith university, Gold Coast) because it was so dirty, loud, expensive etc. BUT they did get free tickets for the social stuff! although they all said they would have done it differently if they could.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They walked us through it altogether at the first formal gathering with the inspector/deen and so on

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: student administration online and in person, alumnis

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i was very successful, the only problem is that you have to mix and match courses and it isn't guaranteed that they fit together schedule wise

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: get help from someone as the alumnis!!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the academic level wasn't satisfying and people had a vibe of "let's just get it over with and pass", it wasn't very motivating. Also I had a teacher who gave us very personal takes (conspiracies) on academic subjects

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: it was third year courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: we didn't have as many lectures or homework but a lot more assignments. Instead of one final exam we were tested throughout the semester

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
2003PHM - drug discovery and development
2213THS - Culinary tourism
2305ENV - Marine Megafauna
3810ESC - Advanced analytical chemistry

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: marine megafauna!! it was super interesting with a passionate teacher and excursions

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: roadtrips!! haha super expensive to go explore but so worth it

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: the supermarkets were approx same as in denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: they had everything!! theater clubs, orchestra club, sports clubs, surfing and diving clubs! and dinner nights every Tuesday:0 (free food) and also they gave free food away like pasta and meatballs every Wednesday

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the running clubs!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go on small roadtrips or hiking trips!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: pretty easy! the most difficult thing for me was to wake up at 5:00 in the morning sometimes to catch sunrise (because that is a thing in Australia!)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: talk with the people in your class! and/or join a social club! I got my best friends from class (chemistry and biology)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: waking up early:0 haha, and it was a veryyyy sporty culture

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the social aspect and a very active lifestyle

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: be open and try to join as many social gatherings as possible no matter what kind!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: apply for a lot of sholarships

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: to meet so many special and like minded people from around the globe!!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To always be social haha

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
